dataset.name: Java Intermediate
dataset.description: Java in depth: OOP, exceptions, collections, generics, lambdas and streams, concurrency, and modern Java and the JVM.

questions.question: Which keyword does a Java class use to inherit from another class?
questions.explanation: extends is used for class inheritance, while implements is used for interfaces.

questions.question: Which keyword does a class use to implement an interface?
questions.explanation: A class can implement any number of interfaces.

questions.question: A Java class can extend more than one class.
questions.explanation: Java allows single inheritance of classes. Multiple inheritance of type is available only through interfaces.
The method is overridden in Dog, and the call is dispatched at run time on the real object type, even though the variable is declared as Animal.
A superclass constructor always runs before the subclass constructor body.
A static field is shared by all instances, and the constructor increments it each time an object is created.

questions.question: What does the keyword super refer to inside a subclass?
questions.explanation: super.method() calls the parent's version and super(...) calls a parent constructor.
Overloads are chosen at compile time from the declared type of the argument. The variable o is declared as Object, so f(Object) is used, while the literal "hi" selects f(String).
Fields are not polymorphic. The variable b has type B, so b.name reads B's field. get() is defined in B, so it also reads B's field.

questions.question: Which of these can hold instance fields (state) that differ per object?
questions.explanation: Interfaces can only declare constants (static final fields). Abstract classes can have ordinary instance fields.

questions.question: What does declaring a class final do?
questions.explanation: String is a well-known final class.
An interface can provide a default method implementation, which implementing classes inherit.

questions.question: A Java class can implement several interfaces at the same time.
questions.explanation: This is how Java gets the benefits of multiple inheritance of type.
call() is inherited from Base, but the call to who() inside it is dispatched on the real object type (Sub).

questions.question: What is encapsulation?
options: Hiding an object's internal state and exposing it only through methods
Converting a class to an interface
questions.answer: Hiding an object's internal state and exposing it only through methods
questions.explanation: Making fields private and providing getters and setters is the classic example.
Without equals and hashCode overrides, Object's identity-based versions are used, so two different instances are never considered equal and both stay in the set.

questions.question: The ______ keyword refers to the current object inside an instance method.
questions.explanation: this is useful, for example, to distinguish a field from a parameter with the same name.

questions.question: Which access modifier makes a member visible within its own package and in subclasses?
questions.explanation: protected members are accessible in the same package and in subclasses, even in other packages.

questions.question: Which class is the root of the Java exception and error hierarchy?
questions.explanation: Both Exception and Error extend Throwable.

questions.question: Checked exceptions must be either caught or declared in the method's throws clause.
questions.explanation: The compiler enforces this for checked exceptions such as IOException.

questions.question: Which of the following is an unchecked exception?
questions.explanation: Unchecked exceptions extend RuntimeException and do not have to be declared or caught.
The try block prints A and throws, the catch prints B, and finally always runs and prints C.
The finally block runs before the method actually returns its value, so F is printed first, and then println prints the returned 1.
A return in the finally block overrides the earlier return value from the try block.
Catch blocks are checked in order, and the first one that matches is used, here the specific NullPointerException handler.

questions.question: What must a resource implement to be used in a try-with-resources statement?
questions.explanation: The close() method is called automatically when the block exits.
getMessage returns the message passed to the exception's constructor.
Resources are opened in the order declared and closed in reverse order after the block finishes.

questions.question: A try block can be used with only a finally block and no catch block.
questions.explanation: try-finally is valid. The exception, if any, still propagates after the finally block runs.

questions.question: Which exception is thrown when you execute int[] a = new int[2]; a[2] = 1;?
questions.explanation: Valid indexes are 0 and 1, so index 2 is out of bounds.

questions.question: A method declares that it may throw a checked exception by using the ______ keyword in its signature.
questions.explanation: throw raises an exception, and throws declares one.
Integer.parseInt throws NumberFormatException for text that is not a valid integer.

questions.question: Which collection type does not allow duplicate elements?
questions.explanation: A Set models a mathematical set. Adding an element that is already present has no effect.

questions.question: Which interface stores key-value pairs?
questions.explanation: Map does not extend Collection. It maps unique keys to values.

questions.question: An ArrayList is backed by a resizable array.
questions.explanation: This gives O(1) indexed access, while inserting or removing in the middle takes O(n).

questions.question: What is the time complexity of get(index) on an ArrayList and on a LinkedList respectively?
questions.explanation: ArrayList indexes directly into its array, while LinkedList has to walk the nodes.
A HashSet stores each element once, so the duplicate 2 is ignored.
A TreeSet keeps its elements sorted by their natural order.
getOrDefault returns the supplied default when the key is absent.
A TreeMap keeps its keys sorted, so a comes before b regardless of insertion order.
merge inserts 1 for a new key and combines with Integer::sum for existing keys, a common way to count occurrences.

A famous quirk: removing the second-to-last element during a for-each loop leaves the iterator at the end, so hasNext() returns false and no ConcurrentModificationException is thrown. Removing other elements would throw.
remove(1) removes the element at index 1 (20), and remove(Integer.valueOf(10)) removes the object 10.
List.of returns an unmodifiable list, so add throws UnsupportedOperationException.

questions.question: A HashMap allows one null key.
questions.explanation: HashMap permits a single null key and any number of null values. Hashtable and ConcurrentHashMap do not.
Putting an existing key replaces its value, so the map still has one entry and its value is 2.
ArrayDeque used as a stack: push adds to the front and pop removes from the front, so the last pushed element comes out first.
A PriorityQueue is a min-heap by default, so poll returns the smallest element.
The comparator orders by string length, and reversed() flips it to longest first.

questions.question: A class must implement the ______ interface to define its natural ordering for sorting.
questions.explanation: Comparable<T> declares compareTo, which sorting methods use by default.

questions.question: What is the default load factor of a java.util.HashMap?
questions.explanation: When the number of entries exceeds capacity x load factor, the map is resized (rehashed).

questions.question: What is the main benefit of using List<String> instead of a raw List?
questions.explanation: The compiler rejects adding non-String elements and removes the need for casts when reading.

questions.question: What does type erasure mean in Java generics?
options: Generic type information is removed by the compiler and is not available at run time
Type parameters must be erased manually
questions.answer: Generic type information is removed by the compiler and is not available at run time
questions.explanation: At run time List<String> and List<Integer> are both just List.
Because of type erasure, both lists have the same runtime class, ArrayList.

questions.question: Inside a generic class Box<T>, you can create an instance of T with new T().
questions.explanation: The type is erased at run time, so the JVM does not know which class to instantiate.

questions.question: What can you do with a List<? extends Number> parameter?
options: Read elements as Number, but you cannot add elements (except null)
questions.answer: Read elements as Number, but you cannot add elements (except null)
questions.explanation: The actual element type may be Integer, Double or another subtype, so the compiler cannot guarantee an added value is safe.

questions.question: What does the PECS mnemonic stand for in generics?
questions.explanation: Use ? extends T when you only read from a structure, and ? super T when you only write to it.
The bounded type parameter T extends Comparable<T> lets the method call compareTo. "pear" is greater than "apple", and 9 is greater than 3.

questions.question: List<int> is a valid declaration in Java.
questions.explanation: Type arguments must be reference types. Use List<Integer> and rely on autoboxing.
Raw types bypass generic checks. The Integer 5 was stored in what is declared as a List<String>, so reading it as a String throws ClassCastException.

questions.question: In class Box<T>, the T is called a type ______.
questions.explanation: T is a type parameter, and the concrete type supplied by the user (such as String) is the type argument.

questions.question: What is a functional interface?
options: An interface with exactly one abstract method
An interface with only static methods
questions.answer: An interface with exactly one abstract method
questions.explanation: Lambdas can be used wherever a functional interface is expected, for example Runnable or Comparator.
The lambda doubles its input, and apply(4) returns 8.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?

System.out.println(Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4)
    .filter(x -> x % 2 == 0)
    .map(x -> x * x)
    .collect(Collectors.toList()));
questions.explanation: filter keeps the even numbers (2 and 4) and map squares them.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?

System.out.println(IntStream.rangeClosed(1, 5).sum());
questions.explanation: rangeClosed includes both ends, so the sum is 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?

System.out.println(Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4).reduce(1, (a, b) -> a * b));
questions.explanation: reduce starts from the identity value 1 and multiplies each element.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?

System.out.println(Stream.of("a", "b", "c").collect(Collectors.joining("-")));
questions.explanation: Collectors.joining concatenates the elements using the given delimiter.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?

System.out.println(Stream.of(5, 3, 9, 1).sorted().limit(2).toList());
questions.explanation: The stream is sorted ascending and limit(2) keeps the first two elements.
groupingBy groups the words by first letter, and counting() counts the words in each group.
Streams are lazy. Intermediate operations such as filter do nothing until a terminal operation runs, and there is none here, so only "done" is printed.
A stream can be consumed only once. A second terminal operation throws IllegalStateException.

questions.question: A Java stream can be traversed more than once.
questions.explanation: Once a terminal operation has run, the stream is closed. Create a new stream to traverse the data again.

questions.question: The method reference String::length is equivalent to which lambda?
questions.explanation: A method reference is shorthand for a lambda that just calls the method.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?

System.out.println(Stream.of(List.of(1, 2), List.of(3))
    .flatMap(List::stream)
    .map(String::valueOf)
    .collect(Collectors.joining(",")));
questions.explanation: flatMap turns each inner list into a stream and flattens them into one stream, which is then converted to strings and joined.
orElse returns the fallback when the Optional has no value.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?

System.out.println(IntStream.of(1, 2, 3, 4).average().getAsDouble());
questions.explanation: average() on an IntStream returns an OptionalDouble, and the mean of 1, 2, 3 and 4 is 2.5.

questions.question: The functional interface ______ takes one argument and returns a boolean.
questions.explanation: Predicate<T> is used by filter and similar operations.

questions.question: Which interface represents a task that can be executed by a thread and returns no value?
questions.explanation: Runnable declares run(). Callable returns a result and can throw checked exceptions.

questions.question: Which Thread method starts a new thread of execution?
questions.explanation: start() creates the new thread and calls run() in it.

questions.question: Calling run() directly on a Thread object starts a new thread.
questions.explanation: Calling run() just executes the method in the current thread like a normal method call.
join() makes the main thread wait until the other thread has finished, so T is printed before M.

questions.question: What does the synchronized keyword provide?
questions.explanation: Only one thread at a time can hold the lock, and changes made inside are visible to the next thread that acquires it.
Both threads increment the shared counter inside a synchronized block, so no updates are lost.
incrementAndGet adds 1 and addAndGet adds 5, so the value is 6. AtomicInteger makes each update atomic without explicit locks.
The executor runs the Callable on a pool thread, and Future.get() waits for and returns the result.

questions.question: What is a deadlock?
options: Two threads writing the same variable
A thread that runs too slowly
Two or more threads each waiting forever for a lock held by another
questions.answer: Two or more threads each waiting forever for a lock held by another
questions.explanation: Acquiring locks in a consistent order is the usual way to avoid deadlocks.

questions.question: What does the volatile keyword guarantee for a field?
options: That only one thread can access it
That all operations on it are atomic
Writes are visible to other threads, but compound operations like count++ are not atomic
That it is stored on the stack
questions.answer: Writes are visible to other threads, but compound operations like count++ are not atomic
questions.explanation: Use AtomicInteger or synchronization for read-modify-write operations.

questions.question: Which Map implementation is designed for safe and scalable use by many threads?
questions.explanation: HashMap is not thread-safe, and ConcurrentHashMap allows concurrent reads and updates without locking the whole map.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?

System.out.println(CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(() -> 5)
    .thenApply(x -> x * 3)
    .get());
questions.explanation: supplyAsync computes 5 asynchronously, thenApply multiplies it by 3, and get() waits for the result.

questions.question: java.util.HashMap is thread-safe.
questions.explanation: Concurrent modification of a HashMap can corrupt it. Use ConcurrentHashMap or external synchronization.

questions.question: The ______ modifier on a method allows only one thread at a time to execute it on the same object.
questions.explanation: A synchronized instance method locks on this.

questions.question: In which memory area are Java objects allocated?
questions.explanation: Local variables and call frames live on the stack, while objects live on the heap and are managed by the garbage collector.

questions.question: What does JVM stand for?
questions.explanation: The JVM executes compiled Java bytecode.

questions.question: What does the garbage collector do?
options: Reclaims the memory of objects that are no longer reachable
questions.answer: Reclaims the memory of objects that are no longer reachable
questions.explanation: An object becomes eligible for collection when no live reference can reach it.

questions.question: What is the difference between the JDK and the JRE?
options: The JDK includes development tools such as the compiler, while the JRE only runs programs
The JDK is only for Windows
questions.answer: The JDK includes development tools such as the compiler, while the JRE only runs programs
questions.explanation: Modern distributions ship a JDK, and a separate JRE is rarely needed.
A record automatically generates a constructor, accessors, equals, hashCode and a readable toString.
Records implement equals by comparing their components, so equal values are equal objects.
var lets the compiler infer the type of a local variable (here ArrayList<String>) from the initializer.

questions.question: In which Java version did text blocks (multi-line string literals with """) become a standard feature?
questions.explanation: Text blocks were previewed in Java 13 and 14 and finalized in Java 15.
A switch expression with arrow labels returns a value and does not fall through.
Pattern matching for instanceof tests the type and binds the variable s in one step.

questions.question: Which keyword lists the classes that are allowed to extend a sealed class or interface?
questions.explanation: Sealed types (final in Java 17) restrict their hierarchy so the compiler can check switch statements for completeness.

questions.question: Where does the JVM store class metadata in Java 8 and later?
questions.explanation: Java 8 removed the permanent generation and replaced it with Metaspace.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?

System.out.println("ab".repeat(2) + "|" + "  hi ".strip() + "|");
questions.explanation: repeat(2) duplicates the text, and strip() removes leading and trailing whitespace.

questions.question: Java programs are platform independent because they compile to bytecode that is run by the JVM.
questions.explanation: Each platform has its own JVM, but the same bytecode runs on all of them.

questions.question: What typically causes an OutOfMemoryError?
options: The heap is full of reachable objects, so the garbage collector cannot free enough space
questions.answer: The heap is full of reachable objects, so the garbage collector cannot free enough space
questions.explanation: Typical causes are memory leaks (objects kept reachable by mistake) or simply too small a heap.
Enum constants are numbered from 0, so HIGH has ordinal 1, and values() returns both constants.

questions.question: The JVM component that compiles frequently executed bytecode into native machine code at run time is the ______ compiler.
questions.explanation: JIT stands for just-in-time compilation and is a key reason Java runs fast.
